_general.insight: Apostrophes inside a jq expression wrapped in bash single-quotes terminate the bash string. Contractions like "today's" silently break the hook. Avoid contractions in any `jq -nc '...'` block, or escape with `'\''`.

Running `next build` against a directory that a `next start` process is currently serving from blows up the running server: the rebuild rewrites .next/ chunks with new hashes, but the running process still hands out HTML referencing the old hashes (or the new HTML referencing chunks the process can't serve), so the browser gets HTTP 500 on the first chunk fetch and the page fails to load. `npm run build:web` must bounce the launchd web tier when it's serving from this dir — see `scripts/bounce-web-if-stale.mjs`. Same shape applies to any long-lived asset server whose on-disk artifacts get rewritten under it (Vite preview, webpack-dev-server in non-watch mode, etc.).

lsof's selector flags (`-p`, `-d`, `-u`, `-c`, etc.) default to OR, not AND. `lsof -p PID -d cwd` returns the cwd of every process on the machine, then a `-p`-matched entry somewhere in the middle. To AND them you must add `-a` explicitly (`lsof -a -p PID -d cwd`). Default-OR semantics mean a buggy lsof selector silently returns wrong-but-plausible data, not an error. Prefer reading from authoritative sources where they exist — for launchd processes, `launchctl print` already includes `working directory = …`.

cli/describe.mjs.insight: When a CLI needs to find a user-installed binary (claude, node managed by nvm/asdf, homebrew tools), spawning `$SHELL -lc 'command -v <bin>'` is the universal lookup — it sources the user's interactive dotfiles, so it finds anything their terminal would. Plain `which` from a launchd-spawned or Finder-spawned process misses every shell-managed PATH.

Any spawned long-running child (claude --print, ffmpeg, anything that may hang) needs both an idle watchdog (no stdout for N seconds → SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after a grace period) and a wall-clock ceiling. `proc.on('exit')` alone is a foot-gun — the parent inherits the child's hang. Surface stderr live (clear the spinner line before each chunk) so a hung child still shows its diagnostic noise instead of going silent.

When parsing streaming LLM output across CLI versions whose envelope format may be either full-snapshot-per-turn or token-deltas, dedup at the *consumer* level (Set of already-emitted keys) instead of trying to detect which format the CLI is using. Append everything you see; the per-key Set makes re-processing identical text idempotent. JSONL output (one `{path, description}` per line) is far easier to incrementally parse than a single closing-brace JSON object.

cli/add.mjs.insight: `process.stdin.isTTY` is unreliable inside Claude Code's Bash tool — the agent wraps Bash in a pty, so isTTY returns true even though no human is there to type. Gate interactive prompts on three signals together: an explicit --yes flag, `process.env.CLAUDECODE === "1"` (Claude Code's documented env var), and the isTTY check. Always pair an interactive readline with a wall-clock timeout fallback so a misclassified non-interactive run can't hang forever.

components/LiveDescriptionsContext.tsx.insight: For a stable mutable slot across renders, use `useRef`, not `useMemo(() => ({}), [])`. StrictMode double-renders re-execute useMemo's initializer, so any "set once" object you stash there can be reset on the second pass — the bug only shows up in production after a user reload, not in dev. Reach for useMemo only when you actually want a memoized *computed* value tied to deps.

components/RepoSwitcher.tsx.insight: Index-based arrow navigation needs a client-side stable sort key — never lean on the order the backend happens to deliver. The daemon's repos() sorts by recency, so every agent touch reshuffles the list and a `(idx + 1) % n` next-pointer silently bounces between repos as activity churns. Backends are free to ship lists in whatever order suits them; the consumer that does positional traversal owns sort stability.

cli/service.mjs.insight: `launchctl load -w` returning 0 only means the plist registered — not that the process is listening. KeepAlive can mask a crash-loop by re-spawning a doomed child indefinitely, and the immediate-next CLI call (e.g. `constellation open`) hits a port that nothing accepted yet. Any user-facing `start`-style command needs a post-load poll (TCP probe or cheap HTTP health) with a timeout, otherwise success-exit means nothing to the user.

`launchctl load` on an already-loaded plist exits 0 *and* prints `Load failed: 5: Input/output error` to stderr — the noise reads as a hard failure to users even though everything is fine. Always pre-unload (`launchctl unload`, stdio ignored) before load if you may be hitting a service that auto-started at login under RunAtLoad.

scripts/web-server.mjs.insight: `next start` forks a `next-server` grandchild that does NOT receive SIGTERM forwarded only to the direct child — the grandchild orphans and keeps the port bound after launchctl unload, so `constellation stop` reports success while `:47318` is still listening. Fix: spawn `next start` with `detached:true` (its own process group) and on shutdown send `process.kill(-child.pid, sig)` to signal the whole group. Same trick works for any wrapper that shells into a tool that itself spawns long-lived workers (gunicorn, pm2, supervisord-as-child, etc.).

daemon/registry.ts.insight: For an auto-touched persistent registry, prefer a stat-on-read filter over delete-from-storage when entries can disappear and reappear. Deleting a worktree that the user later recreates would otherwise force them to re-register; hide-on-read self-heals. The few `existsSync` calls per /repos request are cheap compared to the user-experience cost of stale or wrongly-deleted entries.

daemon/lifecycle.ts.insight: When the user rejects a Claude Code Agent tool spawn at the prompt, agent-start has already fired but no agent-stop or SubagentStop ever will — Claude Code does not (yet) emit a cancellation hook. A periodic TTL sweep is the only reliable cleanup. `lastActiveAt === startedAt` is the cleanest proxy for 'never ran' because every touch path bumps lastActiveAt, but not every touch sets currentPath (Bash/Grep have no file_path).

Claude Code emits no 'session ended' event when the user closes their terminal — Stop fires per-turn, not per-session. Without a TTL sweep that includes idle main agents, every `claude` invocation leaves a __main.json that the daemon will keep reporting as alive forever, producing visual duplicates as old sessions accumulate. Pair the sweep with lazy resurrection on next touch (handleTouch already creates the entry from scratch if missing) so an over-eager TTL is harmless — the user sees their session reappear the moment they do anything.

components/AgentBubble.tsx.insight: When a CSS-triangle tooltip arrow is built as outer-color + inner-mask, the mask's negative margin must point AWAY from its anchor edge — top-full anchor needs marginTop:-1, bottom-full anchor needs marginBottom:-1. Flipping arrow direction by changing only borderTop→borderBottom without flipping the margin produces a 1-px border seam that is easy to miss in screenshots but visible at zoom.

hooks/sse-registry.ts.insight: When sharing a long-lived connection across hook instances with refcounting, give the close path a small grace period (≈100 ms) before tearing down. React 19 StrictMode dev double-mounts and brief route-transition unmount/remounts both flicker refcount through zero — without the grace period you pay reconnect cost on every legitimate consumer remount.

Cache the most recent payload per (url, event) at the registry level and replay synchronously to new subscribers. The daemon's SseBroker already replays current state on connect, but a *second* hook subscribing to an existing shared connection won't get a fresh on-connect snapshot — the cache is what closes that gap. Without it, a freshly-mounted component stares at empty state until the next event.

components/ConstellationOverlay.tsx.insight: Inline-arrow ref callbacks fire cleanup with null on EVERY render (because the function reference changes), not just on unmount. If your cleanup deletes per-element state, you will silently churn that state every snapshot tick. Either return a cleanup function (React 19), memoize the ref callback per stable key, or simply do not delete in the cleanup branch and prune state elsewhere.

components/AgentOverlay.tsx.insight: A child with position: absolute; bottom: 100% must be parented to a fixed-size element, not the outer transform/opacity wrapper. The outer wrapper has willChange:transform,opacity and no fixed height, so a bottom-100% child whose own height affects the parent's height creates a circular sizing dependency. Parent the bubble to the inner ICON_SIZE-square relative div instead — bottom: 100% then resolves to a fixed 28px regardless of bubble height, and opacity still cascades from the outer wrapper through the inner div.

app/page.tsx.insight: A context provider lifted to serve a new consumer must wrap every site that calls its hook, not just the original consumer's subtree. When the new consumer lives in a sibling branch (e.g. a header component while the existing consumer is the page body), wrapping only the existing block leaves the header outside the provider and the new consumer throws 'must be used inside Provider' on first render. The lift only succeeds if it encloses *all* call sites — sketch the tree and trace each hook caller before edits.
